paragraphs: Friend, here's what this passage teaches me: when the heart turns from the LORD, the trouble that follows is no accident. The text says plainly that the LORD raised up Hadad against Solomon, and then God raised up Rezon too (1 Kings 11:14, 23). And the reason the LORD gives is that they "have forsaken Me to worship Ashtoreth the goddess of the Sidonians, Chemosh the god of the Moabites, and Milcom the god of the Ammonites" (1 Kings 11:33). Turning away from God is serious, and this chapter doesn't pretend otherwise.

But watch what the LORD does in the middle of it. He says, "Nevertheless, I will not take the whole kingdom out of Solomon's hand," and He keeps one tribe "for the sake of My servant David" (1 Kings 11:34, 32). I think that is MERCY, baker, mixed right into the hard news. He also says He will humble David's descendants, "but not forever" (1 Kings 11:39). God keeps His word to David even when the people He made that word to have wandered off.

Now look at Jeroboam, because the promise comes with an IF. The LORD says, "If you listen to all that I command you, walk in My ways, and do what is right in My sight," then "I will be with you" (1 Kings 11:38). A gift from God is not a license to coast. So here's the question for you, friend: what has God already put in your hands, and are you walking in His ways with it? This kingdom story is NOT done yet, so keep your apron on.
